practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single behavior. RATIONALE: Easier root-cause identification. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for single Act operation and single Arrange-Act-Assert. DECISION RULES: Only one primary Act (lista0.imprime()) and assertions all relate to 'empty list and printing' behavior -> compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must not depend on each other. RATIONALE: Enables any-order execution. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of setup/teardown or use of only local variables. DECISION RULES: No shared mutable state or numbered test naming; test uses only local variables and helper createLista(). -> compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Provide happy path and error scenario tests. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: At least two tests per method: success and error (e.g., assertThrows or @Test(expected)). DECISION RULES: Only one test method present and it exercises the happy path/empty-case only; no exception or invalid-input test found -> non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Test boundaries like empty or zero. RATIONALE: Boundaries reveal off-by-one and range bugs. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for empty, zero, negative, max values. DECISION RULES: Test explicitly checks empty list (vazia) and behavior of imprime() on empty list -> compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Eliminate duplication via helpers. RATIONALE: Improves maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of helper methods/constants. DECISION RULES: Uses createLista() and captureOutput() helpers (from scaffolding) rather than duplicating setup -> compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests short and simple. RATIONALE: Reduces bugs in tests. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Method length and absence of loops/complex conditionals. DECISION RULES: Method is short (<20 lines) linear, no loops/branches -> compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should verify multiple properties. RATIONALE: Catches deeper faults. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Multiple meaningful assertions about result. DECISION RULES: Test asserts emptiness before and after printing and that printed output is not null (>=2 properties) -> compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid @Ignore/@Disabled and commented-out tests. RATIONALE: Keeps suite active. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of @Ignore/@Disabled or commented out tests. DECISION RULES: No @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test found -> compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Link tests to requirements. RATIONALE: Facilitates impact analysis. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Annotations or Javadoc referencing requirement IDs. DECISION RULES: Class Javadoc includes 'Requirement reference: REQ-001' -> compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Non-functional tests separated or identified. RATIONALE: Performance/security need dedicated tests. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of explicit performance/security tests (e.g., @Test(timeout=...)). DECISION RULES: @Test(timeout = 4000) is present which is explicit timing constraint -> compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should describe scenario and expected outcome. RATIONALE: Improves readability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Descriptive naming patterns like method_condition_result. DECISION RULES: Method is named 'test1' (generic) and does not describe scenario -> non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Avoid verbose auto-generated tests and generic names. RATIONALE: Generated tests are hard to maintain. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for auto-generated comments or repetitive names like test0,test1. DECISION RULES: Test name 'test1' matches auto-generated naming convention; no explicit generator comments but name indicates generation -> non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should show thoughtful design (Given-When-Then or BDD naming). RATIONALE: Test-first/design-led tests are preferable. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Given-When-Then comments or BDD naming. DECISION RULES: The method contains 'Given' and 'When & Then' comments indicating design intent -> compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should exercise public APIs not internals. RATIONALE: Reduces brittleness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: No reflection or private-field checks. DECISION RULES: Test calls public methods (vazia, imprime) and uses helpers, no reflection -> compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Use clear, specific assertions with messages. RATIONALE: Easier diagnosis on failure. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Specific assertion methods and descriptive messages. DECISION RULES: Assertions include descriptive messages and use specific assertion methods (assertTrue, assertNotNull) -> compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain 'why' and be minimal. RATIONALE: Avoid clutter/outdated comments. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for excessive comments or commented-out code. DECISION RULES: Comments present are concise Given/When & Then and class-level Javadoc exists; no commented-out code -> compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid randomness/time dependency. RATIONALE: Prevent flakiness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: No Random(), System.currentTimeMillis(), Thread.sleep() usage. DECISION RULES: Test contains none of those constructs; deterministic -> compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests must not modify shared state without cleanup. RATIONALE: Avoid inter-test interference. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of @After cleanup for persisted resources or absence of persistent actions. DECISION RULES: Test only uses local objects and does not persist data or modify static state -> compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Use @Tag/@Category to organize tests. RATIONALE: Enables selective runs. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of @Category/@Tag annotations. DECISION RULES: Class annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class) -> compliant.
